correctness.rationale: Every Dyck path has exact area deficit twice its down-before-up inversion count. The reverse-down-count staircase bijection identifies the partition normalization, with excluded partitions only at size at least n. Deterministic padding preserves the defect labels and establishes squared overlap Z_n/Z_m. The trace-normalized Pauli second moment equals Hilbert–Schmidt purity, yielding a dimension-free 4 alpha Lipschitz bound on the 2 alpha moment; the diagonal-Pauli Jensen inequality yields its positive P(q)^(-2 alpha) lower bound. This makes the log Lipschitz uniformly and proves both the finite thermodynamic limit and the explicit q^(n/4) error. Independent small-n enumeration via verify.py agrees. No inference from finite tests to infinity is made.

value.rationale: Finite-size numerics for the high-area deformed Fredkin phase suggest bounded magic, but do not justify a thermodynamic limit of an exponentially large nonlinear Pauli sum. The theorem gives an explicit controlled infinite-volume limit at all real orders greater than one, together with an exponential finite-volume error and explicit product bound. This is a useful rigorous bridge to thermodynamic comparison and finite-chain approximation; it deliberately leaves positivity and exact value open.
